  • done completion-event-wakeups — Completion-event wakeups for the pi plugin: the pi chat session should be told when tasks finish instead of having to ask 'check the graph state'. Today the plugin (worksgood-pi/) shells out to wg on demand and the only push surfaces are wg msg/chat-inbox (daemon-side, not delivered to a live pi session) and the new viz panel (a view, not a wake). Deliverables: (1) DESIGN: docs/design-pi-completion-wakeups.md covering the event taxonomy (terminal transitions: done/failed/blocked/waiting-on-human; which tasks matter: top-level/no-parent tasks and any failure, versus every task), the wake primitive on the pi side (pi.sendMessage to inject a session message the agent sees and can act on, ctx.ui.notify for a lightweight ping) and its honest limit (a pi session is turn-based: the plugin can make the information present and visible; document whether/when it can trigger an actual turn), the subscription/dedup model (persisted cursor so a transition is announced once), multi-instance fan-out (several pi sessions attached to one daemon each keep their own cursor), and the config surface (plugin-side settings with safe defaults: failures always; completions top-level by default; per-session quiet toggle). (2) MINIMAL SLICE: implement the polling watcher first (interval read of graph state via the existing wg backend - no daemon protocol change needed), emitting a deduped wake message on qualifying transitions, configurable, with the daemon-push/event-stream path documented as the follow-up (the backend already notes the WG_DAEMON_SOCKET IPC client as future work). Message content must be actionable: task id, title, status, completion summary/receipt reference, and the note that wg tools are available for detail - never a bare 'something changed'. (3) Tests: unit tests for transition detection + dedup/cursor persistence + config gating (fake graph snapshots, no live daemon); one integration check against a real graph with a scratch pi session if feasible. Reuse: worksgood-pi/src/wg-backend.ts (exec host, WG_DAEMON_SOCKET note), viz-snapshot.ts/viz-readmodel.ts (graph reading), the existing plugin test setup. ## Validation - [ ] docs/design-pi-completion-wakeups.md committed with the taxonomy, wake primitive + its limit, dedup model, multi-instance story, config defaults - [ ] Minimal slice works: a task completing in a watched graph produces exactly one actionable wake message in the session; a repeated poll never re-announces it - [ ] Config gating verified (failures always; completions top-level by default; quiet toggle honored) - [ ] Plugin tests green; cargo test --lib green; fmt/clippy clean; worktree clean

  • done concierge-guided-pi — Concierge-guided Pi onboarding: make (attended, interactive) walk a brand-new user from zero to a working automation route, with Pi readiness as the first-class step since WG is embedded in the Pi model plane. Build on the interactive tier-selection flow from setup-collects-strong. Flow: (1) PI DETECTED? If the pi executable is missing, print the exact install command (npm install -g @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent, Node 20+ prerequisite) and exit cleanly with 'rerun worksgood setup after installing Pi' — no partial state, matching the existing ATTENDED_TTY / Pi-unavailable fail-clean style. (2) PROVIDER AUTHENTICATED? Run pi's own credential readiness check (pi auth check or equivalent non-interactive probe) across the providers pi exposes; if none is authenticated, print the guided login instruction (run , then /login <provider>, e.g. openrouter — Pi owns the OAuth flow, WG never sees keys) and exit cleanly for the user to return. (3) MODEL RESOLVABLE? Once authenticated, verify at least one model resolves via Pi's offline registry (reuse the existing bounded preflight style; never live-call). (4) Then continue into the interactive strong/weak tier prompts from setup-collects-strong. Every gate is fail-clean with the exact next command printed; no step ever writes config, installs packages, or stores credentials on WG's side — Pi owns auth, WG only detects readiness. Pin the gate matrix with unit tests (pi missing / pi present + no auth / auth + no resolvable model / all green) using injectable probe results, and a smoke scenario for at least the pi-missing and no-auth gates via the fake-pi fixture. ## Validation - [ ] cargo test --lib green; new gate-matrix unit tests pass - [ ] Smoke scenario covers the early gates via the sanctioned harness bridge - [ ] cargo fmt --check + clippy clean; README/quickstart updated to describe the guided flow
